note: A beginner guitar week at 20 minutes a day: a short hands warm-up, chord changes over a strum-along, A minor pentatonic position 1 returning in five new forms (slow, roots, faster, in E, from memory), and every day ending on something musical. Each step says what to press and where to look.

plan.title: Week 1: position 1 and clean changes
plan.summary: A minor pentatonic position 1 from first notes to improvising, with G-C-D and power chord changes in time, plus a tune a day.

days.theme: Position 1 meets G, C and D

exercises.title: The spider
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 1st fret, every string, 60 bpm
exercises.why: One finger per fret wakes up all four fingers before you need them.

sections.text: Press Play. Play fingers 1 2 3 4 on frets 1 to 4 of the low E, one note per click. Move up a string each time, all the way to the high E. Then come back down.

exercises.title: G, C and D in time
exercises.focus: G-C-D-G changes · down strums at 60 bpm
exercises.why: G, C and D are the I, IV and V of G major, so these three changes open up hundreds of songs.

sections.text: The shapes
Press a chord box to hear the chord. Fret each shape as shown, then pick the strings one at a time to check they ring. Switch between the shapes slowly, in any order.
In time
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord to play. Strum down on every beat, one bar per chord. Use beat 4 to get to the next chord.

exercises.title: Position 1 at 60
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · position 1 · 60 bpm, then the roots
exercises.why: Position 1 is home base for lead guitar: every note sits under your fingers at the 5th fret.

sections.text: Up and down
Press Play on the click. Play the position from the low {{1}} up to the high E string, then back down, one note per click.
Only the roots
Now only the three {{1}} notes (A) are in play. Hop between them low to high, then in any order you like.

exercises.title: First phrases
exercises.focus: Position 1 over drums in A · end on A
exercises.why: Improvising with a few notes is how the position becomes music, not a pattern.

sections.text: Press Play on the band. Play short phrases from position 1, with a gap after each. End your phrases on a {{1}}.

exercises.title: Spider, new order
exercises.focus: Fingers 1324 from the 3rd fret, 60 bpm
exercises.why: Changing the finger order makes each finger move on its own.

sections.text: Press Play. This time the order is 1 3 2 4, starting at the 3rd fret. Go up every string, then back down. Keep it slow enough that every note rings.

exercises.title: A5, D5, E5
exercises.focus: Power chords A5-D5-E5 · quarter notes at 70 bpm
exercises.why: A power chord is only a root and a 5th, so one shape moves anywhere.

sections.text: One shape, three places
Press a chord box to hear it. All three chords are the same shape, moved to a new string or fret. Move between them at your own pace. Let only the two fretted strings ring.
In time
Press Play. The lit block shows the chord. Strum it down once per beat, one bar each.

exercises.title: Position 1: roots and 5ths
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · position 1 · 1 and 5 lit
exercises.why: The two notes of a power chord are also in position 1, which links your riffs to your solos.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play position 1 up and down at 70. Then play only the ringed {{1}} and {{5}} (A and E), low to high and back.

exercises.title: A five-note tune
exercises.focus: Sol Fa Mi Re Do in C, from tab
exercises.why: Short tunes from tab train your hands to find the notes you hear in your head.

sections.text: A tune walking down from Sol to Do. Press Play to hear it. Then play along from the tab.

exercises.title: Position 1 at 70, then 80
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · position 1 · 70 → 80 bpm
exercises.why: Speed comes from small steps up in tempo once the slower one feels easy.

sections.text: At 70
Press Play on the click. Play position 1 up and down at 70, starting on the low {{1}}.
At 80, from the middle
Press Play on the faster click. Now start on the {{1}} on the D string. Go up to the top, down to the bottom, then back up to where you started.

exercises.title: One-minute changes: G and C
exercises.focus: G-C changes · best count in one minute
exercises.why: G to C is the change that trips most beginners, so counting it shows it getting faster.

sections.text: Change from G to C and back for one minute, one strum per chord. Count your clean changes. Rest, then try to beat your count.

exercises.title: Do Mi Sol tune
exercises.focus: Do Mi Sol Mi Do in C on the neck
exercises.why: A tune on the home chord's notes shows you where a melody sits around the C chord.

sections.text: Press Play. The tune uses only {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} (C, E, G). Play along in the neck view, then switch the view to tab.

exercises.title: Call and response in position 1
exercises.focus: Two-bar phrases in A · position 1 · 80 bpm
exercises.why: Answering your own phrase is the simplest way to make a solo go somewhere.

sections.text: Press Play on the band. Play a two-bar phrase, then rest for two bars. Answer it with a phrase that starts the same way but ends on a {{1}}.

exercises.title: The spider, higher up
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 5th fret, 70 bpm
exercises.why: At the 5th fret the frets are closer together, so you can push the tempo a little.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play fingers 1 2 3 4 from the 5th fret, up every string, then back down.

exercises.title: G-Em-C-D strumming
exercises.focus: Down, down-up, up-down-up · G-Em-C-D at 70 bpm
exercises.why: One strum pattern held steady over the changes is what makes chords sound like a song.

sections.text: The pattern on one chord
Try the pattern on G only: down, down-up, up-down-up. Count "1, 2 and, and 4 and" out loud to place each strum.
Over the changes
Press Play. The same pattern, one bar per chord. The lit block shows the chord to play.

exercises.title: Sol La Sol
exercises.focus: A tune with La in G, from tab
exercises.why: La, one step above Sol, gives many folk tunes their lift.

sections.text: Press Play to hear it. Then play along from the tab: Sol La Sol Mi Do. When it feels easy, switch the view to the neck.

exercises.title: Position 1 phrases over A
exercises.focus: Position 1 · phrases ending on C, then on A
exercises.why: The note a phrase ends on changes how finished it sounds.

sections.text: Press Play on the band. End a few phrases on {{b3}} (C). Then end a few on {{1}} (A). Switch between the two. Which ones sound finished?

exercises.title: Spider, 1324
exercises.focus: Fingers 1324 from the 1st fret, 70 bpm
exercises.why: Low on the neck the frets are widest, so this is where the spider builds reach.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play fingers 1 3 2 4 from the 1st fret, up every string, then back down.

exercises.title: E5, G5, A5 riff
exercises.focus: Power chords E5-G5-A5 · 80 bpm
exercises.why: These three are the power chords of E minor, so they fit today's scale.

sections.text: Press Play. The lit block shows the chord. Strum it down on every beat, one bar each. For a chunkier sound, try resting your palm on the strings near the bridge.

exercises.title: E minor pentatonic, two places
exercises.focus: E minor pentatonic · open position, then position 1 at the 12th fret
exercises.why: Position 1 is a shape, not a place: move it to have the scale in any key.

sections.text: Open position
Press Play on the click above. Play E minor pentatonic in open position from the low {{1}} (open E) up, then back down. Every open string is in the scale.
The same notes at the 12th fret
The shape you know from A, moved to the 12th fret: the open position again, an octave higher. Play it up and back, starting on the {{1}}.

exercises.title: Improvise in E
exercises.focus: Open E minor pentatonic over drums
exercises.why: Open strings ring under fretted notes, which is why E is a favourite key for guitar solos.

sections.text: Press Play on the band. Mix fretted notes with open strings. End your phrases on the open low {{1}}.

exercises.title: The spider at 80
exercises.focus: Fingers 1234 from the 3rd fret, 80 bpm
exercises.why: A small step up in tempo shows the week's progress in your fingers.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play fingers 1 2 3 4 from the 3rd fret, up every string, then back down.

exercises.title: G, C, D: the count
exercises.focus: G-C and C-D one-minute changes
exercises.why: Counting again shows how far the changes have come since day 3.

sections.text: One minute of G to C, then one minute of C to D, one strum per chord. Count your clean changes. Compare them with your count from day 3.

exercises.title: Position 1 without the chart
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · position 1 from memory at 80
exercises.why: Playing a shape without looking is the test that it is really yours.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play position 1 up and down without looking at the neck below. Then check against it. Last, play only the {{1}} notes from memory.

exercises.title: A longer tune
exercises.focus: A Sol-stage tune in G, tab then neck
exercises.why: A longer tune asks you to remember phrases, not single notes.

sections.text: Learn it from tab
Press Play to hear it. Then play along from the tab, one phrase at a time.
Play it through
Now the whole tune in the neck view, a little faster. If you slip, keep going with the app.

exercises.title: G-Em-C-D, full pattern
exercises.focus: Strum pattern over G-Em-C-D at 80 bpm
exercises.why: The week's chords at a faster tempo, to hear how far they have come.

sections.text: Press Play. Strum down, down-up, up-down-up, one bar per chord. The lit block shows the chord to play.

exercises.title: Position 1 in A and E
exercises.focus: Minor pentatonic position 1 · A, then E at the 12th fret
exercises.why: One shape in two keys back to back shows you know the shape, not the frets.

sections.text: Press Play on the click. Play position 1 in A up and down, starting on the {{1}}.
Now the same shape at the 12th fret, in E, starting on its {{1}}.

exercises.title: Jam over Am and G
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic position 1 over Am-G
exercises.why: Two chords and one position make a real jam, the kind you can play with friends.

sections.text: Land on the roots
Press Play. Improvise in position 1. Land on {{a}} when Am comes round. Land on {{g}} when G comes round.
Free
Same backing. Now play whatever you like from the position. Try the call and response from day 3.

exercises.title: Your tune, for the record
exercises.focus: Day 6's tune in G at 75 bpm
exercises.why: Recording a tune you learned this week gives you something to compare next week against.

sections.text: Press Play to play day 6's tune along with the app. Then record a take on your phone.
